name: two_speaker_overlap
doc: Two speakers on one mic (crosstalk knob): a bystander's words bleed into the primary speaker's finals, so the rolling 30-word window sometimes fuses two speakers' sentences into one blended window. The blend contaminates the extractor's input — a clean claim ('Octopuses have three hearts') arrives fused with the bystander ('did you get the parking validated') and the window text no longer grounds the claim cleanly, so one claim is LOST to contamination. This is known-degraded: single-mic speaker separation is not yet built; the fixture pins the contamination-recall loss so a diarization/VAD fix can be measured against it. Claims that arrive in a clean window still recover and air.

finals.text: Okay so I want to tell you something wild.
Octopuses have three hearts did you get the parking validated.
The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.
no I did not sorry keep going.
Honey basically never spoils they found edible honey in Egyptian tombs.
